# AGENTS.md

<!-- layer1:start · generated by the harness · do not edit by hand -->

## Verification

1. **Verify before asserting, and with whatever consumes it.** Never take a
   file's word about the environment: **run the tool that reads it and trigger
   what it controls.** What cannot be checked stays `❓ pending`, said out loud.

   _Asking is not enough: `pnpm config get` answered `42` for a key that does
   not exist, and `true` for one that changed nothing._

2. **"Done" means verified by CI, not asserted.** What has not passed the gate
   stays pending, and that is said. **A test only verifies if it can fail:** its
   expected value comes from the requirement, never from the code under test —
   neither its output pasted back nor its logic repeated.

   _A green on your machine only proves your machine; a value copied from the
   code, only the code._

## What the AI does not decide

3. **`.env`, credentials and real data dumps: neither read without explicit
   permission, nor committed.** What the agent reads **enters the
   conversation**, and from there it does not come back. `.env.example` is what
   travels.

4. **The AI installs and configures nothing on its own**: it proposes, the owner
   decides.

   _An install or a config change lands in everyone's lockfile and CI, and
   neither shows in the diff the agent presents._

5. **Nothing destructive without a `--dry-run` first**, showing what would be
   deleted.

   _A `git clean -fd` took three unrecoverable directories._

6. **The AI commits; the person decides the push.** Local commits pile up until
   the go-ahead, **and one go-ahead covers one push**, not the next ones.

7. **No AI trace in commits or output**: no `Co-Authored-By`, no "Generated
   with…".

   _Tools add it by default. History says what changed and why, not with which
   tool._

8. **Conventional Commits, in English**: `type(scope): summary`, with `!` for a
   breaking change. The types: `feat` · `fix` · `docs` · `style` · `refactor` ·
   `perf` · `test` · `build` · `ci` · `chore` · `revert`. The body carries
   **only** the list of changes and the reason for each — the how is already in
   the diff.

## The environment

9. **An agent session has no Node auto-switch.** The hook lives in the shell
   profile and a non-interactive session never loads it: the session runs on
   whatever Node it **inherited when it was launched**, and `cd` into another
   project does not change it.

   **Start the session from a terminal already on the repo's version** — enter
   the directory, let fnm/nvm switch, then launch the agent. **One session per
   project.**

   _If that was not done, activate it on every invocation: `fnm use <major>`
   then the command. `fnm exec --using=N pnpm` does not work on Windows — `pnpm`
   is a `.cmd` and `fnm exec` only launches real executables._

10. **pnpm, never npm.**

_`npm install` leaves a `package-lock.json` next to `pnpm-lock.yaml`, and two
installers disagree in silence._

11. **pnpm settings live in `pnpm-workspace.yaml`**; `.npmrc` carries registry
    and authentication only — from pnpm 11 anything else there is ignored, and
    pnpm 10 still reads it, so it works today and stops on upgrade. Every repo
    with dependencies sets `minimumReleaseAge` there.

## Continuity

12. **State lives in `docs/SESSION.md`**, written **when a task closes** — at
    session close there is no context left — and **overwritten**: git keeps the
    history. Nothing the code or `git log` already tells goes in.

13. **The reasoning lives in `docs/DECISIONS.md`**, append-only. A decision that
    changes **is not edited**: another is appended revising it, and the old one
    is **marked, never deleted**. Knowing what was believed is part of the
    record.

14. **An exception is declared** in the project's `AGENTS.md`, with its reason
    and its scope; failing silently is not an option. Does not apply to
    security, AI traces or pushing.

## Naming

15. **File names, configuration keys and identifiers in English.**

## Knowledge that is not in this file

16. **Skills are per project.** `npx autoskills` installs them into
    `<repo>/.claude/skills/`, which is **git-ignored and rebuilt** like
    `node_modules`; **`skills-lock.json` is committed** — it carries each
    skill's source and hash, and it is what makes three machines rebuild the
    same set. **The developer runs `autoskills`, not the agent** — `npx`
    downloads a package, and installing is not the agent's call.

_Global skills in `~/.claude/skills/` are the machine's, not the project's._

17. **Official docs and MCPs are consulted and never silenced**, at the
    **installed** version — from the lockfile, not the `^` range. **Context7 is
    the one every project uses**: `resolve-library-id`, then `query-docs` at
    that version. If the MCP does not answer, say so instead of pretending it
    was consulted.

## Review

18. **When work is reviewed, this is the shape.** `architect` before building;
    `reviewer` and `security` over what was built, **read-only**; `tester` to
    verify. Run them whenever you want, together or on their own.

Guide for any coding agent (Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex…) working in this repository.

## How it is organized

Monorepo of three **independent** packages: **`backend/`** (Express + MySQL), **`frontend/`**
(Next.js) and **`video/`** (Remotion). There is no pnpm workspace: **each package is installed and
run on its own**, with its own `node_modules`, its own `package.json` and its own lockfile.

This file holds what is common. What is specific to each package lives in its own file, which **is
read in addition to this one, not instead of it**:

| Scope       | Instructions         | Documentation (outside git)  |
| ----------- | -------------------- | ---------------------------- |
| whole repo  | this file            | `docs/`                      |
| `backend/`  | `backend/AGENTS.md`  | `docs/`, «Backend» sections  |
| `frontend/` | `frontend/AGENTS.md` | `docs/`, «Frontend» sections |
| `video/`    | this file            | —                            |

All the documentation lives in the root `docs/` (since 2026-11-26): `README.md` (architecture),
`DECISIONS.md` (one ADR series, with an index on top) and `TODO.md`, each with a general part and
«Backend» and «Frontend» sections; plus `ROADMAP.md` (the order of the pending work),
`SESSION.md` (where we left off) and `_archive/` (retired documents, for reference only). **The
same thing is never written in two sections.**

**Declared exception (rule 14):** `docs/` is ignored by git, so rules 12 and 13 are met **only on
this machine**. Reason: the repository is public and that documentation is not. Scope: `docs/`,
temporarily, by the owner's decision (2026-11-17).

## Security

**L3** — estimated on 2026-11-17: login with user accounts (local and OAuth), personal data and
money, own backend; if security is not adequate, a leak of personal data can cause serious harm to
third parties.

**Areas:**

- Authentication, Session, JWT tokens → `backend/controllers/auth/`, `backend/services/auth/`,
  `backend/middlewares/authenticateToken.ts`, `backend/models/auth/`, `frontend/app/api/auth/`
- OAuth/OIDC → `backend/config/oauth.ts`, `frontend/app/(public)/auth-callback/`
- Authorization → `backend/repositories/`
- API → `backend/routes/`, `backend/middlewares/`, `frontend/app/api/proxy/`
- Validation / errors → `backend/validators/`, `backend/middlewares/sanitizeMiddleware.ts`,
  `backend/utils/`
- File upload → `backend/routes/import/`, `backend/services/import/`
- Cryptography → `frontend/lib/crypto.ts`, `frontend/stores/cryptoStore.ts`,
  `frontend/hooks/useEncryption.ts`, `backend/controllers/crypto/`, `backend/services/auth/pinService.ts`
- Communication → `backend/config/db.ts`
- Configuration / DevOps → `backend/index.ts`, `frontend/next.config.ts`, `backend/config/config.ts`,
  `backend/.env.example`
- Data protection / privacy → `backend/controllers/ai/`, `backend/services/ai/`

🔴 **This repository is PUBLIC: be careful about what is exposed.** Neither the `AGENTS.md` files
nor any other versioned file may contain security architecture details, environment variable
names, database schemas or local paths. That context lives in the `docs/`.

## Where the model goes wrong

- **A prompt with many tasks at once** → execution scatters → work with **concise, individual
  tasks**, one at a time.

## Up-to-date documentation (context7 MCP)

Before proposing code for a dependency of any of the packages, look up in context7 the
documentation for the **exact version installed** in that package — not the latest published, not
the one you remember.

This repo is, by far, **the one that strays furthest from the model's defaults**, and in opposite
directions within the same tree: the backend runs **Express 5** (ahead) and **ESLint 8 with
`.eslintrc.json`** (behind), and the frontend **Tailwind 3** (behind) and **ESLint 9 with
`eslint.config.mjs`**.

### Flow

1. `resolve-library-id` with the library name.
2. `query-docs` with the resolved ID, the version from the table and the specific topic.
3. If the exact version is not indexed, use the closest minor **below** it and state explicitly in
   the answer which version you consulted.

Check that it is available before relying on it: `claude mcp list` (or `opencode mcp list` in
OpenCode) → `context7` Connected. If it is not, **say so in the answer** and continue from your own
knowledge; do not pretend you consulted it.

⚠️ **The version pin does not always filter.** Verified in another repo with Express: querying the
v4 ID still returned v5 snippets. **If a context7 result contradicts a pitfalls table, the table
wins.**

⚠️ **Snippets are not written for `strict`.** The API they describe is usually right, but they omit
null guards and fail the typecheck. The symptom is misleading: it looks like a version problem and
it is not.

### ⚠️ Three packages, three different environments

- **`engines.node`: backend and frontend `>=24.22.3 <25`, video undeclared.** With `engineStrict`
  on, using the wrong Node makes the install fail. The minimum is the most recent security patch of
  24: it is raised by hand with each Node security bulletin.
- **React differs between packages** (frontend 19.2.3, video 19.2.4): do not assume that what
  compiles in one compiles in the other.

### Shared by backend and frontend (source of truth: `node_modules`, not the `^` ranges)

| Package         | Version      | Note                           |
| --------------- | ------------ | ------------------------------ |
| `typescript`    | **6.0.3**    | ⚠️ Not 7: see below            |
| `eslint`        | ⚠️ different | 🔴 8.57.1 back · 9.39.5 front  |
| `zod`           | **4.6.7**    | ⚠️ v4, the same in both        |
| `@noble/hashes` | **2.0.1**    | ⚠️ v2                          |
| `@types/node`   | **25.0.5**   | ⚠️ Ahead of the Node that runs |

- **`eslint`: two versions and two formats.** The backend runs **8 with `.eslintrc.json`**: do not
  convert it to flat config. The frontend runs **9 with `eslint.config.mjs`** (flat,
  `defineConfig()`) since phase 3; not 10, because `eslint-plugin-react`, `-import` and
  `-jsx-a11y` do not support it yet.
- **`typescript` 6, not 7**: TypeScript 7 does not yet ship the compiler's JavaScript API and
  `typescript-eslint` only supports `<6.1.0`; with 7, the lint in `verify` breaks. 6 errors on any
  option that 7 removes (`TS5107`): **do not silence it with `ignoreDeprecations`**, change the
  option. `@typescript-eslint` is on 8.x in both packages.
- **`zod` 4**: top-level `z.email()`, not `z.string().email()` (deprecated). Nothing from the v3
  API.
- **`@noble/hashes` 2**: the subpaths and the API changed from v1.
- **`@types/node` 25 with Node 24 in backend and frontend**: if `tsc` accepts something from the
  Node runtime, verify it against the **Node 24** docs, not against what autocomplete allows. **Do
  not "fix" it on your own initiative**: it is the owner's decision.

### `video/`

| Package    | Version     | Note                                                                                                     |
| ---------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `remotion` | **4.0.242** | With `@remotion/cli` at the same version. The manifest declares a lower range; what is installed is this |
| `react`    | **19.2.4**  | ⚠️ Different from the frontend (19.2.3)                                                                  |

## Checks before calling something good

**Backend and frontend run Vitest inside `pnpm run verify`**, together with the lint and the
typecheck or the build. Coverage is partial: there are no integration tests against a real
database, and the SQL queries are checked by hand. Each package defines in its `verify` what is
checked, and its exceptions are in its `AGENTS.md`. The CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs that
`verify` in `backend/` and `frontend/`, each with its own Node and its own pnpm. `video/` has
neither a `verify` nor tests.

## context7 limits

- It is for **verifying**, not for migrating. Do not apply version changes or "modernize" code that
  works unless explicitly asked. In particular: **do not propose upgrading to Tailwind 4 or
  migrating the backend's ESLint to flat config.**
- If the current docs recommend a different pattern from the one the repo already uses, **do not
  rewrite**: point it out and follow the existing convention unless the owner decides otherwise.
- **Reactive and bounded** use: only new or modified code in the task at hand. Never as a sweep
  ("review the whole project against the current docs").
- Do not use it for business logic, refactors or your own debugging — only for the library's API.

## Conventions

- Markdown format: Prettier defaults. GitHub-flavored table style.
